raj: Heads-up - noticed a spike in partial-rejects for fncall toolhooks around 09:03. Console shows a sudden increase in 'coerce_errors' and some requests got routed to fallback with billing tags.

maya: Ugh. Wasn't that the strict schema canary we flipped last week?

raj: Yes. Canary id=sv-17, validator=fncall-typed-strict. Most rejects look like this: ```
2026-03-23T09:03:12Z WARN validator=fncall-typed-strict fncall=tool.invoice_create status=PARTIAL_REJECT reason=TypeMismatch details=\"expected object, got array for field 'line_items'\"
2026-03-23T09:03:12Z INFO router reroute=degen-fallback billing_tag=charged
```

ajex: (typo) alex: If line_items is sometimes an array that's valid upstream; our adapter used to coerce arrays->objects in permissive mode. Strict prevented coercion, flagged PARTIAL_REJECT and router treated as hard.

tammy: We have two bugs interacting: 1) validator signals PARTIAL_REJECT but our routing policy maps any non-OK to reroute+bill, 2) telemetry exposes only "rejected_count" and not soft vs hard classification.

jess: Can we switch the routing map so PARTIAL_REJECT => routing:shadow or drop-charge? We should avoid billing on partials until human review.

raj: Agreed. Quick fix idea: patch policy: ```yaml
- id: partial-reject-handling
  match: { status: PARTIAL_REJECT }
  action: { reroute: degen-fallback, charge: false, tag: "soft-validate" }
```

maya: Also need console panels: split metric `fncall_rejects_total` into labels `validation_severity=hard|partial|soft` and expose `billed_reroutes_total`. Alert if billed_reroutes_total > 0.001 * fncall_rejects_total during canary window.

observability-bot: New dashboard panel suggested: fncall_rejects_by_severity (timeseries), billed_reroutes_ratio (gauge).

alex: We should also update the adapter to emit `original_payload` sampling for rerouted traces so auditors can see why it failed without replaying. Sampling rate 5% initially.

jess: For rollout UX: can we add a sticky warning in the console when validator canaries are ENABLED that says "canaries may reroute traffic; ensure reroute paths are non-billable and add alerts" with a link to a checklist? PMs kept saying users ignore canary implications.

raj: Action plan: 1) maya flip canary -> soft for sv-17 (doing now). 2) tammy apply policy patch to avoid billing on PARTIAL_REJECT (PR in 30m). 3) jess add dashboard panels + alert (ETA 4h). 4) alex add trace sampling flag + adapter change (ETA next week). 5) raj update rollout checklist doc.

maya: Running command: `/rollout set validator:fncall-typed-strict=soft-canary --id=sv-17`

observability-bot: @maya received rollout change. Applying...

observability-bot: Done. sv-17 set to 30% traffic.

tammy: Opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4987 - adds policy rule + unit tests for charge=false semantics.

alex: After PR merges, can someone trigger a synthetic test: call invoice_create with array line_items and confirm router log shows `charge=false` and trace contains `original_payload` sample id.

jess: I'll draft the console warning copy and ping design for the CTA. Also adding sticky tooltip for canary windows.

raj: Quick customer impact check: how many rerouted calls were billed? estimate ~650 in the 20m spike, across 2 accounts. Low cost but need CS template.

maya: Tammy, can you prepare a CS credit template?

tammy: On it. I'll include tags for accounts + link to incident notes.

raj: Thanks. Let's reconvene after policy patch is live and synthetic test passes.

maya: Thanks team. small follow-up: add e2e test to CI that verifies validator=permissive vs strict behavior for adapter coercion to avoid future surprises.

alex: Good idea. I'll add a test case in `platform/validators/tests/test_fncall_coercion.py`.

raj: Closing notes: prefer non-bill routing for any non-fatal validation failures during canaries and expose explicit metrics. We'll aim to re-enable strict only after telemetry shows <0.01% billed reroutes for 1h. :white_check_mark:
